content.value_statement: Early ideas often miss constraints, alternatives, and success criteria. This skill guides structured questions, option comparisons, and validation before planning or coding.
actual_capabilities: Presents two or three solution approaches with trade-offs.
Uses structured choices for clear decision points.
Builds designs in short sections with validation checks.
Identifies when to revisit earlier brainstorming phases.
Hands approved designs to worktree setup and planning skills when available.
limitations: It does not generate production code by itself.
It depends on user answers for requirements and constraints.
Referenced sub-skills must be installed separately for handoff steps.
It does not prove technical feasibility without workspace inspection.

use_cases.title: Shape a Product Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a rough feature request into goals, constraints, success criteria, and a validated design direction.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Approaches
use_cases.description: Review several architecture options with trade-offs before choosing a path for implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Planning
use_cases.description: Validate the design before creating a detailed work plan for a developer or AI coding agent.

prompt_templates.title: Start From Rough Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to turn this rough idea into a clear design: [idea]. Ask me one question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to compare two or three approaches for [feature]. Highlight trade-offs, complexity, and success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for selecting a direction.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to build a validated design for [system]. Present architecture, data flow, errors, and tests in sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for structured design review.

prompt_templates.title: Move From Design to Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill for [initiative], then hand off to planning after I approve the design. Include assumptions and unresolved decisions.

output_examples.input: I want to add team invitations to my app.
output: Clarifying question about invite flow, roles, and expiration needs.
Comparison of direct email invites, link-based invites, and admin-created accounts.
Validated design summary with components, data flow, and testing focus.

output_examples.input: Help me decide how authentication data should be stored.
output_examples.output: The skill presents storage options with security and usability trade-offs, then asks you to select the best fit.

output_examples.input: I have a design, but users keep adding new constraints.
output_examples.output: The skill returns to earlier brainstorming phases, updates constraints, and revises the design before planning continues.

best_practices: Answer each question with concrete constraints and success criteria.
Choose one approach after reviewing trade-offs.
Validate each design section before moving to planning.
anti_patterns: Skipping clarification and asking for a full plan immediately.
Combining multiple approaches without resolving trade-offs.
Treating the handoff steps as required when no implementation will follow.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It prepares a validated design before coding or implementation planning begins.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when an idea is unclear, risky, or missing requirements before implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with architecture decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares two or three approaches and explains trade-offs for each one.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: The core brainstorming flow works alone. Worktree setup and planning handoffs depend on separate skills.

faq.question: How does it handle feedback?
faq.answer: It presents designs in sections and asks for validation before continuing.

faq.question: Is it suitable for nontechnical ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. The question and validation process can support product, workflow, and planning decisions.
